Forecast Discussion

Cold high pressure centered in New England is wedged down the east side of the Appalachians today. Low pressure has developed off the Southeast coast and it will move north along the coast today and then NW across the central and eastern Carolinas Wednesday night and Thursday. An upper level low is over western TN and KY and it will move across KY and the OH Valley through Friday.

With clouds and rain moving in for the second half of the afternoon, temperatures will not rise as much as usual, leading to a cold, raw day.

Rain is steady and heavy at times overnight. Temperatures slowly rise overnight. The wind is from the east and gusty this afternoon but stronger overnight.

Rain continues into Thursday morning along with gusty winds. Drier air works its way in bringing an end to the rain by afternoon. It remains cold and windy though.

Colder air associated with the upper low moves in Thursday night and Friday morning. There is enough moisture left over that snow showers and flurries develop overnight and continue into Friday. We don't have high confidence in accumulations at this time but light accumulations are possible, especially along the NC/TN border and in the higher peaks. Winds will be strong and gusty from the west and NW Thursday night and Friday.

Things begin to settle Friday night with flurries winding down. High pressure builds in from the southwest Saturday bringing clearing skies, milder temperatures and less wind.

Sunday starts off nice but a cold front moves in quickly from the west. Clouds thicken Sunday afternoon and rain develops Sunday night into Monday morning. The front moves through Monday morning, ending the rain and cooling temperatures. High pressure builds in Tuesday giving us a relatively pleasant day.
